t: Minimum Operations to Equalize Subarrays — Residues, Medians, Persistent Trees
o: Adding/subtracting k preserves each element's residue mod k, so a subarray is equalizable iff all its elements share one residue. Working in units of k, element i becomes qᵢ = (nums[i] − r)/k and making everything equal to target t costs Σ|qᵢ − t|, minimized at the median of the qᵢ. So each query needs: (1) a range residue-equality test (sparse table min/max), and (2) the median and Σ|q − median| over a range — answered with a persistent segment tree keyed by compressed q values, giving k-th selection and prefix count/sum in O(log n). Example: [1,4,7], k=3 → q = [0,1,2]; query [0,2] has median 1, cost 1+0+1 = 2.
k: Residue mod k is invariant ⇒ equality of residues is the feasibility test; otherwise −1.
Cost Σ|qᵢ − t| is minimized at the median; persistent segment trees answer order statistics and partial sums per query in O(log n).

a.i: For each query, check residues directly and sort the extracted q values to find the median and accumulate absolute differences. Clear but O(len log len) per query — too slow at scale, yet perfect for validating the fast solution.
s: For query [l,r], verify nums[i] % k identical for all i in range, else −1.
Collect qᵢ = (nums[i] − r)/k, sort, take middle as median.
a.t: O(Q · n log n) worst case — sorting each queried range

a.n: Approach 2: Sparse Table + Persistent Segment Tree (Optimal)
a.i: Precompute a sparse table over residues for O(1) equality tests, and persistent segment trees over compressed q-values so version r+1 minus version l represents the range; walk down once for the median and once for count/sum of values ≤ median to get the cost.
s: Build residue min/max sparse tables; build persistent trees inserting qᵢ sequentially.
Walk versions to find the median value m (k-th of tot elements).
Second walk accumulates count/sum ≤ m; cost = m·cl − sl + (stot − sl) − m·(tot − cl).

c.python:
class Solution:
    def minOperations(self, nums: List[int], k: int, queries: List[List[int]]) -> List[int]:
        n = len(nums)
        res = [x % k for x in nums]
        mn = [res[:]]; mx = [res[:]]
        j = 1
        while (1 << j) <= n:
            h = 1 << (j - 1)
            mn.append([min(mn[-1][i], mn[-1][i+h]) for i in range(n - (1 << j) + 1)])
            mx.append([max(mx[-1][i], mx[-1][i+h]) for i in range(n - (1 << j) + 1)])
            j += 1
        vals = [(nums[i] - res[i]) // k for i in range(n)]
        qs = sorted(set(vals)); V = len(qs); idx = {v: i for i, v in enumerate(qs)}
        L, R, C, S = [0], [0], [0], [0]
        def add(prev, lo, hi, p, v):
            node = len(L)
            L.append(L[prev]); R.append(R[prev])
            C.append(C[prev] + 1); S.append(S[prev] + v)
            if lo < hi:
                mid = (lo + hi) >> 1
                if p <= mid: L[node] = add(L[prev], lo, mid, p, v)
                else: R[node] = add(R[prev], mid + 1, hi, p, v)
            return node
        roots = [0]
        for v in vals:
            roots.append(add(roots[-1], 0, V - 1, idx[v], v))
        ans = []
        for l, r in queries:
            jg = (r - l + 1).bit_length() - 1
            if min(mn[jg][l], mn[jg][r - (1 << jg) + 1]) != max(mx[jg][l], mx[jg][r - (1 << jg) + 1]):
                ans.append(-1); continue
            A, B = roots[l], roots[r + 1]
            tot = C[B] - C[A]; stot = S[B] - S[A]
            kk = (tot + 1) // 2; lo, hi = 0, V - 1; xa, xb = A, B
            while lo < hi:
                mid = (lo + hi) >> 1
                if kk <= C[R[xb]] - C[R[xa]]: xa, xb = L[xa], L[xb]; hi = mid
                else: kk -= C[R[xb]] - C[R[xa]]; xa, xb = R[xa], R[xb]; lo = mid + 1
            m = qs[lo]; cl = sl = 0; ya, yb = roots[l], roots[r + 1]; lo, hi = 0, V - 1
            while lo < hi:
                mid = (lo + hi) >> 1
                if m <= mid: ya, yb = L[ya], L[yb]; hi = mid
                else:
                    cl += C[L[yb]] - C[L[ya]]; sl += S[L[yb]] - S[L[ya]]
                    ya, yb = R[ya], R[yb]; lo = mid + 1
            cl += C[yb] - C[ya]; sl += S[yb] - S[ya]
            ans.append(m * cl - sl + (stot - sl) - m * (tot - cl))
        return ans

a.t: O((n + Q) log n) — persistent tree builds once; each query does two O(log V) walks
a.sp: O(n log V) persistent nodes plus O(n log n) sparse tables

w: Derive the residue invariant and median optimality first — the data structures are then standard. Common pitfalls: forgetting the −1 feasibility branch, off-by-one in median selection for even lengths (either middle element gives the same cost), and 64-bit cost sums. Follow-up: point updates (replace persistence with a BIT of sorted structures or a segment tree of multisets), or minimize the maximum deviation instead of total operations.
